verdict.rationale: Lovable's first-party docs describe Git sync to a repository the user owns on GitHub or GitLab, kept in sync automatically. Changes flow both ways: local commits pushed to the repo sync back into Lovable, and branches and pull requests are supported. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of bidirectional sync reliability (e.g., conflict handling).

support.subject: As a developer, I can sync my project to my own GitHub repository and keep changes flowing both ways

citations.quote: Git sync connects a Lovable project to a repository you own on GitHub or GitLab, and keeps the two in sync automatically
Clone the repository, edit and commit locally, and push. Your changes sync back into Lovable.
you can export and sync your project to GitHub: back up your code, review changes in pull requests, work locally in your IDE, test features on branches, and deploy outside Lovable
